clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old Chinese man on long-term hemodialysis with a history of secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) presented with hypercalcemic crisis (albumin-corrected calcium 3.96 mmol/L) and symptoms including restless legs, nausea, constipation, and weakness. Despite previous treatment with cinacalcet, PTH remained inappropriately elevated (197.3 pmol/L) despite severe hypercalcemia, indicating autonomous parathyroid function with an increased calcium-PTH set-point. Imaging workup revealed negative neck ultrasound but positive Tc-99m sestamibi scan localizing a hyperfunctioning gland, confirmed by CT as a 2.5×1.9 cm mediastinal mass. Thoracoscopic excision revealed a 2 cm well-encapsulated mass with microscopic confirmation of parathyroid chief cells. Postoperatively, calcium normalized (2.12→2.30 mmol/L) and PTH normalized (21.41→18.63 pmol/L), with resolution of restless legs and gastrointestinal symptoms, confirming tertiary HPT arising from ectopic mediastinal parathyroid tissue.
